enhanced_information: The case presents a 16-year-old woman with primary amenorrhea, normal secondary sexual characteristics, and normal estradiol and testosterone levels. The findings of vaginal agenesis, absence of the uterus, and normal ovaries are consistent with Rokitansky syndrome (Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome), which is characterized by congenital absence of the uterus and vagina while maintaining normal ovarian function. The absence of the left kidney is also a common association with this syndrome. Other options such as Morris syndrome, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, polycystic ovarian syndrome, and Kallman syndrome are ruled out based on the absence of testicular tissue, lack of androgen excess, absence of polycystic changes, and no signs of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, respectively. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is Rokitansky syndrome.
analysis: The clinical presentation of primary amenorrhea in a 16-year-old woman with normal secondary sexual characteristics, normal levels of estradiol and testosterone, agenesis of the vagina, absence of the uterus, and normal ovaries suggests a diagnosis of Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome, also known as Rokitansky syndrome. This condition is characterized by the congenital absence of the uterus and vagina, while ovarian function remains intact, which aligns with the findings in this case. The absence of the left kidney is also consistent with the renal anomalies that can accompany this syndrome. Other options such as Morris syndrome (Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome) would typically present with abnormal testosterone levels and male secondary sexual characteristics, while congenital adrenal hyperplasia and polycystic ovarian syndrome would not explain the absence of the uterus and vagina. Kallman syndrome primarily affects the sense of smell and is associated with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, which does not fit this presentation. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis is Rokitansky syndrome.
